title: The Mysterious King of Salem
subtitle: The Book of Melchizedek — Genesis 14:17-20 — Melchizedek's first appearance
description: An introduction to Melchizedek, the mysterious king-priest who appears in Genesis 14 to bless Abraham after the slaughter of the kings. We examine his dual office of king and priest, the significance of the bread and wine, the meaning of his name, and the theological import of Abraham's tithe, with reflections from John Owen and Matthew Henry.

title: A Priest Forever
subtitle: The Book of Melchizedek — Psalm 110:4 — David's prophetic declaration
description: A study of Psalm 110, the most frequently quoted psalm in the New Testament, with special attention to verse 4: 'Thou art a priest for ever after the order of Melchizedek.' We examine the divine oath, the eternal priesthood, and the implications for Christ's ministry, drawing upon John Owen, Thomas Goodwin, and Stephen Charnock.

title: Without Father, Without Mother
subtitle: The Book of Melchizedek — Hebrews 7:1-3 — The eternal priesthood
description: A verse-by-verse study of Hebrews 7:1-3, examining the inspired interpretation of Melchizedek's names (King of Righteousness, King of Peace), the theological significance of his absent genealogy, and the debate over whether Melchizedek was a theophany or a historical type. With extensive commentary from John Owen and John Calvin.

title: Greater Than Abraham
subtitle: The Book of Melchizedek — Hebrews 7:4-10 — The superiority of Melchizedek
description: A study of Hebrews 7:4-10, where the writer demonstrates Melchizedek's superiority over Abraham and the Levitical priesthood through the acts of tithing and blessing. We examine the principle of federal headship — how Levi paid tithes 'in Abraham' — and its connection to the doctrines of original sin and imputed righteousness.

title: A Better Covenant
subtitle: The Book of Melchizedek — Hebrews 7:11-22 — The need for a new priesthood
description: A study of Hebrews 7:11-22, examining the writer's argument that the Levitical priesthood was never intended to be permanent, that its impermanence implies a change in the law, and that Christ's priesthood — established by divine oath, not genealogical descent — inaugurates a better covenant of which He is the surety and guarantor.

title: The Unchangeable Priesthood
subtitle: The Book of Melchizedek — Hebrews 7:23-28 — Christ's eternal intercession
description: The climax of Hebrews 7: Christ's unchangeable priesthood, His ability to save to the uttermost, His perpetual intercession, and the perfection of His once-for-all sacrifice. We examine the Greek word 'aparabatos' (untransferable), the comfort of Christ's ceaseless intercession, and reflections from Owen, Goodwin, and Richard Sibbes.

title: Melchizedek in Puritan Theology
subtitle: The Book of Melchizedek — How Owen, Goodwin, and others interpreted the type
description: A survey of how the great Puritan theologians understood and applied the Melchizedek typology. We examine John Owen's exegetical precision, Thomas Goodwin's devotional warmth, Stephen Charnock's emphasis on divine immutability, and William Gouge's practical application — drawing lessons for our own approach to Scripture.

title: King of Righteousness, King of Peace
subtitle: The Book of Melchizedek — The full typology fulfilled in Christ
description: Our concluding study gathers every thread of the Melchizedek typology and traces its complete fulfillment in Christ. We examine how Jesus is the true King of Salem, the true Priest of the Most High God, the one who brings bread and wine, the one who blesses the faithful, the King of Righteousness and Peace — the eternal antitype to whom every shadow pointed.
